note: The paper's own integrated model (Figures 1-2): ten distinguishing characteristics (representational fidelity; learner interaction) linked via intermediate outcomes (identity, presence, co-presence) to five learning affordances (FE).

Adopts Gibson's (1979) coinage and Greeno's (1994) operative definition: 'an affordance relates attributes of something in the environment to an interactive activity by an agent who has some ability' (FAITHFUL-Dalgarno & Lee, p.21, quoting Greeno).
3-D VLEs facilitate tasks leading to enhanced spatial knowledge representation of the explored domain (FE, p.18).
3-D VLEs facilitate experiential tasks impractical or impossible in the real world; nuclear-plant, astronaut, forestry-operator training examples (FE, p.19).
3-D VLEs facilitate tasks leading to increased intrinsic motivation and engagement, via personalization/choice and flow (FE, p.19).
3-D VLEs facilitate tasks leading to improved transfer of knowledge/skills through contextualization of learning (FE, p.21).
3-D VLEs facilitate tasks leading to richer/more effective collaborative learning than 2-D alternatives (FE, p.23).

Six sub-characteristics: realistic display, smooth view/object motion, consistent object behavior, user representation, spatial audio, kinaesthetic/tactile feedback; folds in Brna's social fidelity for multi-user contexts (FE, Table 1).
Four sub-characteristics: embodied actions, embodied verbal/non-verbal communication, control of environment attributes, construction/scripting of objects (FE, Table 1).
'Being there together' with geographically dispersed users; explicit extension of the social-presence tradition (Short/Williams/Christie 1976) (FAITHFUL-Dalgarno & Lee, p.14).
Adopts Slater's immersion/presence distinction; presence treated as a consequence of fidelity + interactivity, not an independent property (FAITHFUL-Dalgarno & Lee, p.13).
Co-presence defined and linked to CMC social-presence tradition; treated as a consequence, not an independent characteristic (FAITHFUL-Dalgarno & Lee, p.14).
Immersion defined per Slater as objective/measurable system properties; explicitly refused status as a unique 3-D-VLE property (FE, p.13).
Learner-interaction category: embodied actions, communication, environment control, construction/scripting (FE, Table 1).
Avatar-mediated identity construction via Dickey's presence/representation/embodiment triad (FAITHFUL-Dalgarno & Lee, p.14-15, citing Dickey 2002).
Affordance 3: personalization/choice-driven intrinsic motivation (Cordova & Lepper 1996) (FE, p.19).
Affordance 3 explicitly invokes Csikszentmihalyi's flow construct (FAITHFUL-Dalgarno & Lee, p.19).
Affordance 4: contextualization/transfer grounded in situated-learning theory (FE, p.20-21).
Affordance 2: experiential/skill-training tasks impractical in reality (FE, p.18-19).
Six-item sub-taxonomy of visual, behavioral, and sensory fidelity characteristics (FE, Table 1).
Source of the adopted immersion/presence distinction, cited directly (FAITHFUL-Dalgarno & Lee, p.13, citing Slater 1999, 2003, 2004).
Cited within the paper's discussion of early presence/immersion terminology debates that motivated its adoption of Slater's distinction (FE, p.13).
Source of the 'transparent interface' / immersion-fidelity-participation framework synthesized into the ten-characteristic taxonomy (FAITHFUL-Dalgarno & Lee, p.12, quoting Hedberg & Alexander 1994).

note: Source of the representational fidelity / immediacy of control / presence framework, later extended by Brna (1999) (FE, p.12-13).

Source of the operative affordance definition quoted directly by the authors (FAITHFUL-Dalgarno & Lee, p.21, citing Greeno 1994).
Source of 'flow', invoked to explain Affordance 3's motivation/engagement mechanism (FE, p.19, citing Csikszentmihalyi 1990).
Source of the media-vs-method critique grounding the paper's explicit rejection of simple 2-D-vs-3-D media-comparison designs (FAITHFUL-Dalgarno & Lee, p.24, citing Clark 1983, 1994a, 1994b).
Source of the three-aspect (presence/representation/embodiment) account of avatar-mediated identity construction (FAITHFUL-Dalgarno & Lee, p.14-15, citing Dickey 2002).
Situated-learning theoretical foundation cited for Affordance 4's contextualization/transfer claim (FE, p.21, citing Lave & Wenger 1991).
Social-constructivist grounding cited for Affordance 5's collaborative-learning claim (FE, p.21, citing Vygotsky 1978).
Source of the affordance-matching methodology (matching learning-task affordance requirements with ICT affordances) the paper concurs with (FAITHFUL-Dalgarno & Lee, p.21, citing Bower 2008).

Explicitly rejects simple 2-D-vs-3-D media-comparison designs as unable to separate learning design from media, per Clark's argument; a methodological stance rather than an empirical condition (FAITHFUL-Dalgarno & Lee, p.24).

target: desktop-3D sufficient proxy for IVR <-> IVR carries unique affordances
note: (P/anticipatory-application) This paper is the cluster's earliest source of the affordance-optimism pole later tested against by Strand C's media-comparison experiments (Colin et al.; Merchant; Makransky-equivalence) and Strand E's reviews; the paper itself is desktop-3D-focused and does not claim IVR-specific affordances.
Dickey's three aspects (presence, representation, embodiment) illustrated as the mechanism by which 3-D-VLE users construct online identity (FAITHFUL-Dalgarno & Lee, p.14-15).

(P/anticipatory-application) The exemplar bank's 'Action-affordance requests' and 'shared dimension' sections register student desire for exactly the interactivity/collaboration affordances (Affordances 2 and 5) this model predicts; its monotony/value-skepticism sections register the predicted failure mode when affordances are not harnessed by design.

(P/anticipatory-application) Mark's 'Focus' quadrant (high engagement x high challenge) is a plausible psychological cousin of the flow-based Affordance 3 this paper invokes, though the two frameworks classify along different axes (levels vs. structures) and should not be treated as equivalent.

target: Part III dissertation (affordance-harnessing framing for VLE design gaps)
note: (P/anticipatory-application) The paper's own prediction that un-harnessed affordances yield 'minimal unique learning benefits' offers Part III a ready theoretical frame for reading the VLE exemplar bank's monotony/value-skepticism material as a design-harnessing failure rather than a media failure.
